title: Finite-coefficient open direct image with a uniform Tor interval
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $U,X$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open $k$-immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $\ell^n1_A=0$ for some $n\ge1$, given its discrete topology and its continuous-map condensed ring $\underline A$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. For $T=U,X$, use $A_T=p_T^*\underline A$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and the ordinary unbounded derived category of internal $A_T$-modules and total right derived module direct image [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. There exists an integer $d_j\ge0$, depending on $j$ and $A$ but not on $K,a,b$, such that for all integers $a\le b$ and every $K$ which is constant-model bounded constructible [sk-def-sfb-constructible] and has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ against all degree-zero $A_U$-module objects [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude], $Rj_*K$ is constant-model bounded constructible and has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+d_j]$ against all degree-zero $A_X$-module objects. The assertion includes the zero ring and zero complex and imposes no separable-closedness hypothesis on $k$.

proof.text: First suppose $A\ne0$. Every ideal of $A$ is a finite set, hence generated by its elements, so $A$ is Noetherian. Every finite $A$-module $M$ is finitely presented: choose a surjection $A^r\to M$ from a finite list of generators; its kernel is a subset of the finite set $A^r$ and is therefore finitely generated. The element $\ell^n$ is invertible in $k$ because $p\ne\ell$. Both $U$ and $X$ are qcqs by the separated finite-type-over-a-field criterion. The qcqs-morphism permanence lemma then makes $j$ qcqs. These are the hypotheses needed for the constructible comparison and bounded-below direct-image comparison below.

Use the finite-discrete module-object/ordinary-coefficient equivalence on $U$ and $X$, denoting its derived forward functors by $E_T$. It identifies $p_T^*\underline A$ with the constant ring sheaf, preserves each Tor interval against all degree-zero modules, and identifies finite constant local models and bounded constructibility. Thus $H=E_U(K)$ is an ordinary bounded constructible pro-étale $A$-complex with Tor interval $[a,b]$. The constructible comparison gives a bounded constructible étale $A$-complex $L$ and an isomorphism $H\simeq\nu_U^*L$. Apply the Noetherian Tor-interval comparison to $L$: its inverse-image interval is $[a,b]$, so the étale interval of $L$ is also $[a,b]$. In particular $L$ belongs to both $D^+$ and $D^-$.

proof.text: Choose $d_j=\operatorname{cd}(j)$. The open-finiteness amplitude lemma says that this is finite and that $R^qj_{\mathrm{et},*}F=0$ for every $A$-module sheaf $F$ and every $q>d_j$. The definition of cohomological dimension makes $d_j$ a nonnegative integer. This choice uses only the fixed morphism, so it is independent of $K,a,b$. In particular this is a relative direct-image bound; no bound on $\operatorname{cd}(k)$ is used.

Put $Q=Rj_{\mathrm{et},*}L$ in the ordinary unbounded module derived category. For every finite $A$-module $M$, step 1 gives finite presentation. The finite-constant projection theorem applies: $A$ is Noetherian, $L\in D^-$, and step 3 bounds all higher module direct images. It gives the canonical isomorphism
$$Q\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_X\simeq Rj_{\mathrm{et},*}(L\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_U).$$
Now apply the arbitrary-field open Tor-bound theorem with $V=U$, $T=X$, $e=d_j$, and this $L\in D^+$. Its input Tor interval, uniform higher-direct-image bound and finite-module projection hypotheses have all been verified. It concludes that $Q$ has Tor interval $[a,b+d_j]$ against every étale module sheaf, not only finite or constant test sheaves.

source.place: Paragraph (3), finite-coefficient open case; projection and all-module Tor test spelled out by the cited existing lemmas

proof.text: The finite-coefficient open-image finiteness theorem applies to $L$: the schemes are of finite type over the field $k$, $j$ is open, $A$ is finite, and its annihilator $\ell^n$ is invertible in $k$. Consequently $Q=Rj_{\mathrm{et},*}L$ is bounded constructible. This supplies the constructibility needed to apply the Noetherian Tor-interval comparison on $X$.

The ordinary total-derived/bounded-below comparison, applied to the qcqs morphism $j$ and bounded-below $L$, gives
$$Rj_{\mathrm{proet},*}H\simeq Rj_{\mathrm{proet},*}
u_U^*L\simeq
u_X^*Q.$$
These are the ordinary unbounded derived functors on the bounded-below inputs, as specified by that comparison. Constructible comparison carries the bounded constructible $Q$ to bounded constructible $
u_X^*Q$. The Noetherian interval comparison carries its étale Tor interval $[a,b+d_j]$ to the same interval against every pro-étale module sheaf. The internal/section-module derived comparison identifies $E_X(Rj_*K)$ with the ordinary direct image $Rj_{\mathrm{proet},*}E_U(K)$: its underived equivalence is the section-action equivalence of step 2, with the constant-ring identification there. Finally the finite-discrete coefficient equivalence reflects bounded constant-model constructibility and the full all-module Tor interval. Hence the actual internal module-object $Rj_*K$ has both required properties.

proof.text: If $A=0$, every unital $A_T$-module is zero since $m=1m=0m=0$; take $d_j=0$. For any $A$, the zero complex has zero derived direct image and all its tensor products vanish, so it satisfies every asserted interval. If $U$ is empty then its module category is zero and this case applies. For nonzero $A$ the single $d_j$ selected in step 3 works for all $a\le b$ and all $K$ by steps 2--6. No step has assumed that $k$ is separably closed.

It is a 7-step split of a statement-only base item; there is no repair note, and the item is still unsplit live and side-live. I checked each hypothesis of every cited node. Step 1: the qcqs-over-affine and permanence lemmas make U, X and j qcqs; finite A is Noetherian and finite modules are finitely presented. Step 2: the module-object/ordinary equivalence (same E_T, constant-model Dbc, all Tor intervals), then sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison (qcqs, discrete Noetherian), then det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian (iff on the same [a,b]). Step 3: det-geo-open-finiteness-ii-amplitude(1) gives R^q j_* F = 0 for every A-module sheaf when q > cd(j); def-kun-cd makes d_j ≥ 0 and independent of K. Step 4: lem-sf-projection-finite-constant (Noetherian, D^-, finitely presented M, all-module bound) and then lem-sf-open-tor-bound-arbitrary-field (arbitrary field, D^+, e = d_j) give Tor amplitude [a, b+d_j] against all modules. Step 5: cor-fin-deligne-open-finite-coefficients gives D^b_c. Step 6: the bounded-below total-derived comparison gives ν^* Rj_* ≅ Rj_* ν^*; the Tor/constructibility comparisons apply on X; lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison identifies the internal Rj_* with the ringed one. Step 7: the zero-ring and empty cases. Tested on G_m→A^1 with F_ℓ (shift 1 needed), j = id, A = Z/ℓ^2, A = 0, and k with infinite cd. I found no cycle and no duplicate (grep of all [a,b+…] open Tor nodes).
